# Step-by-step guide to `CLEO/libs/coupldyn_yac` GENERATED BY CLAUDE AI

This walks through everything that happens in `CLEO/libs/coupldyn_yac` (plus the one file it
leans on outside that directory, `libs/configuration/communicator.hpp/cpp`), in the order it
actually executes: build/link, YAC initialisation, coupling definition, end-of-definition, and
the runtime put/get exchange loop. Each step is cross-referenced against the YAC documentation
in `icon-mpim/externals/yac/doc` (also at https://dkrz-sw.gitlab-pages.dkrz.de/yac/) by page/section
name, so you can look up the authoritative description alongside CLEO's actual usage.

## 0. What this directory is

`coupldyn_yac` is one of CLEO's interchangeable "coupled dynamics" backends — the thing that
supplies pressure/temperature/humidity/winds to CLEO's superdroplet model at each coupling step.
Instead of reading dynamics from a file (like CLEO's other backends), this one receives them
live from ICON-mpim over YAC, a coupler library for exchanging and interpolating fields between
different model components running as separate MPI processes/executables.

Directory contents:

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `CMakeLists.txt` | Builds `libcoupldyn_yac.a`, links YAC/YAXT/MPI |
| `cmake/FindYAC.cmake`, `cmake/FindYAXT.cmake` | Locate the pre-built YAC/YAXT libraries and expose `YAC::YAC` |
| `yac_cartesian_dynamics.hpp/.cpp` | The actual YAC calls: grid/point/field/couple definitions, put/get |
| `yac_comms.hpp/.cpp` | Glue between YAC's `CartesianDynamics`/`YacDynamics` and CLEO's generic `Gridbox`/`State` machinery |
| `libs/configuration/communicator.hpp/.cpp` (outside this dir, but load-bearing) | YAC initialisation and component definition, done once before any of the above |

## 1. Build and link (`CMakeLists.txt`, `cmake/FindYAC.cmake`, `cmake/FindYAXT.cmake`)

`CMakeLists.txt` does `find_package(YAC REQUIRED)`, which runs `cmake/FindYAC.cmake`. That module
first requires YAXT, NetCDF and LAPACK (YAC's own dependencies), then looks for `yac_interface.h`,
`libyac.a` and `libyac_mtime.a` under `${YAC_C_INCLUDE_DIR}`/standard search paths (seeded from
`CLEO_YAC_ROOT`, set one level up in the top-level CMake config), and packages everything into a
single imported target `YAC::YAC` that also pulls in `YAXT::YAXT_C`, NetCDF, LAPACK, `fyaml` and
`libm`. `cmake/FindYAXT.cmake` does the analogous thing for `libyaxt_c.a`/`libyaxt.a` and exposes
`YAXT::YAXT_C`/`YAXT::YAXT_Fortran`. `coupldyn_yac`'s own `CMakeLists.txt` then links
`YAC::YAC` and `MPI::MPI_C` privately, and `configuration`/`gridboxes`/`superdrops` publicly (the
libraries it needs for its own header dependencies — `Config`, `Gridbox`, `State`).

This is plumbing, not YAC API surface — YAC docs: `installing_yac` (linked from `overview` /
`yac_libs`) covers configuring/building/installing YAC itself.

## 2. YAC initialisation (`libs/configuration/communicator.hpp/.cpp`)

Before any of `coupldyn_yac`'s own code runs, `init_communicator`'s constructor decides whether
YAC is even in play (`config.get_yac_dynamics().lower_longitude` being set is the signal — the
bubble-case-without-YAC path skips straight to plain `MPI_Init`). When YAC is present:

```cpp
yac_cinit();
std::string component_name = "cleo";
yac_cdef_comp(component_name.c_str(), &init_communicator::yac_comp_id);
yac_cget_comp_comm(init_communicator::yac_comp_id, &comm);
```

This is exactly the **Initialisation Phase** and the **Component Definition** subsection of the
YAC docs' `usage` page (`phase_init`, `phase_def_comp`): `yac_cinit()` initialises the *default*
YAC instance for `MPI_COMM_WORLD` (see `overview` and `yinstance` — CLEO never uses named/multiple
instances, always the default one), `yac_cdef_comp` registers CLEO as a component named `"cleo"`
(this name is what ICON's own `yac_cdef_couple` calls have to match on the other side),
and `yac_cget_comp_comm` hands back the MPI sub-communicator YAC carved out for CLEO's own
processes — that's what CLEO uses for its own internal MPI calls afterward (`comm_size`,
`my_rank`), not `MPI_COMM_WORLD`.

`init_communicator::yac_comp_id` is stored as a static class member so `CartesianDynamics`'s
constructor can retrieve it later via `init_communicator::get_yac_comp_id()` — this is the
`component_id` used in every subsequent `yac_cdef_field` call.

The destructor is deliberately a no-op on the YAC path (`"yac_finalized elsewhere"` — YAC's own
finalisation, `yac_cfinalize()`, happens outside this class, presumably in CLEO's top-level driver
after both dynamics loops have shut down cleanly — not shown in this directory).

## 3. Grid and point definitions (`create_grid_and_points_definitions`, `yac_cartesian_dynamics.cpp` ~L122–188)

Called once from `CartesianDynamics`'s constructor. This is the **Grid Definition** and **Point
Definition** phase (`usage.dox`: `phase_def_grid`, `phase_def_point`).

```cpp
yac_cdef_grid_reg2d(grid_name.c_str(), total_vertices, cyclic_dimension,
                    vertex_longitudes.data(), vertex_latitudes.data(), &grid_id);
```

`yac_cdef_grid_reg2d` is the "regular 2D grid" grid-definition routine — you hand it 1-D arrays of
distinct vertex longitudes and latitudes (`E+1` and `N+1` values respectively for a partition of
`E×N` cells) and YAC forms the full 2-D vertex mesh by permutation, rather than you enumerating
every vertex explicitly (that's what `yac_cdef_grid_unstruct` would require instead — see
`phase_def_grid` for the unstructured variant CLEO doesn't use here).

Three point sets are then defined on top of that one grid, all via the location-tagged point
definition routines described in `phase_def_point`:

- **Cell centers** (`yac_cdef_points_reg2d`, `YAC_LOCATION_CELL`): same trick as the grid itself —
  a 1-D array of cell-center longitudes and one of cell-center latitudes, permuted into the full
  2-D set of cell centers by YAC. This is what `pressure`, `temperature`, `qvap`, `qcond`, and
  `vertical_wind` are defined on.
- **A single combined edge point set** (`yac_cdef_points_unstruct`, `YAC_LOCATION_EDGE`):
  because the horizontal winds live at *different* locations than cell centers (the C-grid
  staggering — `eastward_wind` at E+1 zonal positions × N meridional rows, `northward_wind` at E
  zonal positions × N+1 meridional rows) and those two shapes don't fit the regular-2D permutation
  trick, CLEO builds the coordinates explicitly and registers them with the unstructured-points
  routine instead, which — per `phase_def_point` — just takes literal `x_points`/`y_points`
  arrays in whatever order the caller provides, with no implied structure. **This is the one CLEO
  currently shares between both `eastward_wind` and `northward_wind`** (both fields are defined
  on this same `edge_point_id` — see §5), which is the crux of the wind-coupling bug we've spent
  this whole conversation on: because YAC imposes no ordering of its own, whatever order the two
  row-types are interleaved in when the coordinate arrays are built is exactly the order the
  runtime `get` buffer comes back in, and the current code builds that array with alternating
  row-types (see the earlier discussion in this conversation for the full derivation and fix).
## 4. Interpolation stack (`CartesianDynamics` constructor, ~L318–326)

```cpp
yac_cget_interp_stack_config_from_string_yaml(
    "[{\"nnn\": {\"n\": 1, \"weighted\": \"arithmetic_average\"}}]", &interp_stack_id);
```

This is the YAML-string variant of defining an **interpolation stack** (`interp_stack.dox`, and
the method itself in `interp_methods.dox`): a single-method stack consisting of n-nearest-neighbour
with `n=1`. In practice this makes every `get` a straight nearest-neighbour lookup — the closest
ICON source point's value is copied to each CLEO target point, no actual blending happens with
`n=1` (the `interp_stack` doc's own worked examples all use `nnn` as a *fallback* stage after a
more sophisticated primary method — CLEO uses it as the sole, primary method here, which is the
simplest choice and appropriate for the very coarse idealised bubble grid, but means CLEO gets
whatever the single nearest ICON grid point holds, not an area-weighted or distance-weighted
value).

## 5. Field definitions (`yac_cdef_field`, ~L338–378)

This is `phase_def_field`. Each call binds one or more point sets (here always exactly one, hence
`num_point_sets = 1` everywhere) to a named field on the current component, plus a
`collection_size` — how many "layers" of that field get exchanged together as one unit (YAC's
`put`/`get` buffers are always `[collection_size][horizontal_points]`; per `phase_exchange`,
`collection_size` is typically used for multiple vertical levels of the same variable, which is
exactly how CLEO uses it: `horizontal_fields_collection_size = ndims[VERTICAL]` for
pressure/temperature/qvap/qcond/eastward_wind/northward_wind, and
`vertical_winds_collection_size = ndims[VERTICAL] + 1` for `vertical_wind`, since w lives on cell
*interfaces* — one more level than cell centers).

Seven receive-side fields (`pressure`, `temperature`, `qvap`, `qcond`, `eastward_wind`,
`northward_wind`, `vertical_wind`) and three send-side fields (`temperature_send`, `qvap_send`,
`qcond_send`) are defined this way, all under the `"cleo"` component and a locally-named
`"cleo_grid"`.

## 6. Couple definitions (`yac_cdef_couple`, ~L385–423)

This is `phase_def_couple`. Each call pairs one of CLEO's fields with the correspondingly-named
field on ICON's side (component `"atm"`, grid `"icon_atmos_grid"` — these strings have to match
whatever ICON's own YAC setup calls itself, which lives in ICON's source, not in CLEO):

```cpp
yac_cdef_couple("atm", coupldyn_grid_name, "pressure",
                 "cleo", "cleo_grid", "pressure",
                 coupling_timestep, YAC_TIME_UNIT_ISO_FORMAT, YAC_REDUCTION_TIME_NONE,
                 interp_stack_id, icon_lag, cleo_lag);
```

Every receiving couple uses the single shared `interp_stack_id` from §4, a fixed
`coupling_timestep = "PT30S"`, and `icon_lag = 1`/`cleo_lag = 0` (the lag arguments offset which
model timestep a `put`/`get` on either side is associated with — see the `yac_cdef_couple`
reference entry in `reference.dox` for the precise semantics if you need to tune coupling timing;
CLEO currently hardcodes `PT30S`/these lag values rather than deriving them from `Config`, worth
knowing if you ever change the model's actual coupling interval). Reversing source/target defines
the three send-side couples (`cleo`→`atm`, with `temperature_receive`/`qvap_receive`/
`qcond_receive` as ICON's names for what CLEO calls `temperature_send`/etc.).

## 7. End of definitions (`yac_cset_config_output_file` + `yac_cenddef`, ~L427–432)

`yac_cset_config_output_file("coupling_debug.yaml", ...)` asks YAC to dump the fully-resolved
coupling configuration to a YAML file at end-of-definition (`phase_enddef_write_config`) — this is
the file worth inspecting to empirically confirm point-set sizes/ordering when debugging.
`yac_cenddef()` is the single call that ends the **Definition Phase** and triggers YAC's internal
neighbourhood search and interpolation-weight computation (`phase_enddef`) — after this call
returns, the coupling configuration is fixed and `put`/`get` become valid.

## 8. Post-`enddef` setup (~L434–483)

Three things happen after `yac_cenddef()`:

- **Coupling-direction detection**: `yac_cget_component_metadata_instance` is queried for a
  `"oneway_coupling"`/`"twoway_coupling"` string tag, stored as `yac_coupling_flag` (1 or 2). This
  flag is what later gates whether `send_fields_to_yac`/`receive_fields_from_yac` actually do
  anything (see §11) — it's presumably set from the YAML coupling configuration file, not visible
  in this directory.
- **Buffer sizing**: `yac_cget_grid_size(YAC_LOCATION_CELL/EDGE, grid_id)` asks YAC how many local
  points exist at each location on this process (post-decomposition), and `yac_raw_cell_data`/
  `yac_raw_edge_data`/`yac_raw_vertical_wind_data` — the raw per-level receive buffers `yac_cget`
  writes into — are allocated to match.
- **Target container sizing**: `press`/`temp`/`qvap`/`qcond`/`uvel`/`vvel`/`wvel` (the flattened
  `(horizontal, vertical)` arrays `receive_yac_field` ultimately fills — see §11) are sized here.
## 9. The runtime exchange: receive side (`receive_yac_field`, `receive_fields_from_yac`)

This is `phase_exchange`, the `get` half. For each field, `yac_cget_action` first checks what YAC
expects for this call (`phase_data_exchange_info` — the `YAC_ACTION_*` enum: `NONE`, `REDUCTION`,
`COUPLING`, `GET_FOR_RESTART`, `PUT_FOR_RESTART`, `OUT_OF_BOUND`); CLEO only special-cases
`GET_FOR_RESTART` (skips the `yac_cget` call and logs it), unlike the pattern YAC's own docs show
(`phase_data_exchange_advance_with_exchange` recommends checking for `YAC_ACTION_NONE` and calling
`yac_cupdate` in that case) — worth keeping in mind if you ever see coupling timesteps silently not
advancing. Otherwise `yac_cget(yac_field_id, vertical_levels, yac_raw_data, &info, &error)` performs
the actual redistribute-and-interpolate `get`, filling `yac_raw_data[level][horizontal_point]`
(this matches `phase_exchange`'s own example: buffers are always `[collection_size][...]`, `level`
here standing in for `collection_size`). The subsequent triple loop reshapes that
level-then-point layout into CLEO's own point-then-level flat `target_array`, dividing by
`conversion_factor` along the way (see the earlier detailed line-by-line walkthrough in this
conversation for the exact indexing).

`receive_fields_from_yac()` just calls this once per cell-based field
(temperature/pressure/qvap/qcond/vertical_wind, all consistent because they're all defined on the
unambiguous `yac_cdef_points_reg2d` cell point set) and — currently, incorrectly, per this whole
conversation's debugging — twice more for the two wind fields sharing the interleaved combined
edge point set from §3.

## 10. The runtime exchange: send side (`send_yac_field`, `send_fields_to_yac`)

The `put` half, only exercised when `yac_coupling_flag == 2` (two-way). It reshapes CLEO's flat
`field_data` (point-then-level) into YAC's expected `send_buffer[level][pointset=0][point]` layout
(the mirror image of §9's reshape), then `yac_cput(field_id, ndims_vertical, send_buffer, &info,
&ierror)`. Same `yac_cget_action`/`GET_FOR_RESTART`-analogue check via `YAC_ACTION_PUT_FOR_RESTART`
beforehand. Only `temperature`, `qvap`, `qcond` are sent — CLEO doesn't feed pressure or winds back
to ICON in this setup.

## 11. Gluing into CLEO's generic coupling machinery (`yac_comms.hpp/.cpp`)

`CartesianDynamics` (everything above) and `YacDynamics` (a thin wrapper around it, in the `.hpp`)
are YAC-specific. `YacComms` is what makes that satisfy CLEO's generic `CoupledDynamics`/coupling
comms interface, so the rest of CLEO's SDM loop doesn't need to know YAC exists:

```cpp
void YacComms::receive_dynamics(const GbxMaps &gbxmaps, const YacDynamics &ffdyn,
                                const viewh_gbx h_gbxs) const {
  const int coupling_flag = ffdyn.get_dynvars()->get_yac_coupling_flag();
  if ((coupling_flag == 2) || (coupling_flag == 1)) {
    ffdyn.get_dynvars()->receive_fields_from_yac();
  }
  Kokkos::parallel_for(..., [=, *this](const size_t ii) {
    update_gridbox_state(ffdyn, ii, h_gbxs(ii));
  });
}
```

**This is the actual call site that triggers a `get` each coupling step** — note it calls
`receive_fields_from_yac()` directly, *not* through `YacDynamics::run_dynamics()` (which has the
same call commented out in the `.hpp`, `// dynvars->receive_fields_from_yac();`). That resolves
something flagged as uncertain earlier in this conversation: the commented-out calls in
`YacDynamics::run_dynamics()` and the `CartesianDynamics` constructor are dead/superseded — the
live path is entirely through `YacComms::receive_dynamics`, invoked from wherever CLEO's core SDM
loop calls into its `CoupledDynamics`/comms concept (outside this directory). `send_dynamics` is
the mirror image on the put side, gated on `coupling_flag == 2` only (one-way coupling never
sends).

After the `get`, `update_gridbox_state` is what actually lands the received values into each
`Gridbox`'s `State` (`press`, `temp`, `qvap`, `qcond`, `wvel`, `uvel`, `vvel`), run in parallel
over all gridboxes via `Kokkos::parallel_for` — this is where the (currently wrong) `uvel`/`vvel`
values from §9 propagate into the superdroplet model's actual state.

## Where to go for more

- `usage.dox` (`phase_init` → `phase_final`, sequentially) is the single most useful page for
  cross-referencing anything in this directory — it walks the exact same phase order this guide
  does, with C/Fortran/Python examples for every routine.
- `interp_methods.dox` if you want to understand what other interpolation methods (beyond the
  `nnn` CLEO uses) are available and when they're more appropriate.
- `reference.dox` for the full function/argument reference of every routine mentioned here.
- `page_raw_exchange` (`raw_exchange.dox`) — **not** currently used by CLEO despite the similar
  naming (`yac_raw_data`/`yac_raw_cell_data` etc. are just CLEO's own buffer-naming convention);
  this page describes an entirely different, opt-in YAC feature (`use_raw_exchange` /
  `yac_cget_raw`) where YAC skips interpolation and hands the target process raw source points
  plus weights to interpolate itself. Worth knowing it exists and is unrelated, so you don't
  conflate the two when reading CLEO's variable names.
